summary: The run made reasonable economic and recovery choices, including an early Strike removal and resting before Hexaghost, but accumulated many card rewards and then entered a prolonged boss fight with insufficient survivability. The decisive failure was not simply the final hit: by the late boss turns, HP had fallen to single digits while Hexaghost still had substantial HP, forcing increasingly constrained choices.

lessons.title: Skip more marginal attack rewards
lessons.situation: When Act 1 rewards offer another generic attack after the deck already has several attacks and some damage coverage.
lessons.lesson: Use Skip more often to preserve draw consistency. In particular, avoid taking duplicate or low-impact attacks unless they address a clear current need; a smaller deck makes key defensive and damage cards appear more reliably in difficult fights.
evidence_points: The run accepted nine permanent card rewards, including Clothesline, Twin Strike, two Pommel Strikes, Hemokinesis, and Second Wind.
The final deck contained 21 cards, including four Strikes, four Defends, two Pommel Strikes, and several other attacks.
Hexaghost reached the late fight with 31 HP while the player had only 9 HP, showing that the accumulated deck and combat plan did not produce a sufficiently decisive boss race.
lessons.reasoning: The trajectory does not prove that any single reward caused the loss, but repeatedly accepting rewards—including a second Pommel Strike—created a relatively large Act 1 deck. Future runs should be more selective when a reward does not materially improve the deck's immediate plan.

lessons.title: Reassess the damage-versus-survival line at critical HP
lessons.situation: When HP is in the single digits, the boss is still alive, and several attack and block lines are simultaneously legal.
lessons.lesson: Do not automatically spend the whole turn on partial blocking. Compare every legal sequence for either a near-lethal attack or enough block to survive, especially when the boss is already below roughly one-third health; at minimum, explicitly evaluate attack options such as Bash or Twin Strike before committing to Shrug It Off plus Defend.
evidence_points: On turn 11, with 9 HP, Hexaghost at 31 HP, and 3 energy, the legal alternatives included Defend, Strike, Shrug It Off, Twin Strike, and later Bash; the chosen line was Shrug It Off, Defend, then Twin Strike.
That line left Hexaghost at 21 HP and the player at 9 HP with 9 block, after which the run ended with Hexaghost still alive at 16 HP.
One turn earlier, at 13 HP against Hexaghost at 54 HP, the player chose Defend before playing both Pommel Strikes and ended the turn with only 5 block; the next logged turn began at 9 HP.
lessons.reasoning: The exact incoming damage and best counterfactual line are not fully recoverable, so this is not proof that a particular card would have won. However, the logged states show repeated turns where the player made only incremental progress while approaching lethal danger; future play should explicitly prioritize either a verified kill or a survival threshold rather than defaulting to mixed low-impact lines.
